name: Conformal-Screw Constraint-First MOND (CSCF-MOND)
claimed_mechanism: MOND dynamics is generated by the algebraic constraint C_MOND = D_i[mu(y)D^i chi] - rho = 0, which fixes the chi profile and generates the MOND force law. The lensing slip is supplied by a second algebraic scalar 's' that couples to the spatial conformal factor (spatial_einstein) and acceleration, sourced by a coefficient e^{-y}. Because 's' is strictly algebraic, it possesses no propagating DOF, meaning there is no kinetic normalization to collide with the screened coupling, thereby structurally evading the P7 strong-coupling wall.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit, the chi constraint yields the MOND force law, while the s-field generates a trace-shift in the spatial metric that produces the required off-ray lensing slip (Gamma != 1). Because s is sourced by e^{-y}, the slip vanishes in the Solar System (screening), but is active in galactic regimes. The kinetic terms of the metric remain standard GR, so the theory is not strongly coupled at the high-acceleration end.
inequivalence_argument: Unlike DC-010 (khronometric), this architecture uses no khronon, and the screened preferred-frame coupling is carried by an algebraic scalar rather than a propagating or degenerate vector, avoiding the strong coupling of the longitudinal mode. Unlike DC-001/DC-013 (frameless), it explicitly includes a preferred-frame coupling (acceleration) to break the slip-lock. Unlike DC-014 (stiff vector), the slip is not carried by a timelike vector field.
